$comment: Executive Brief schema 1.0.0 (S0-13). Frozen: see docs/architecture/brief-schema.md for the compatibility and freeze rules. Blueprint §1.3, §4.2, §5.6, §11.
title: Executive Brief
description: One versioned Executive Brief. The same document is rendered by the SwiftUI menu bar, the Blade HTML mail and the PWA; renderers must not diverge in semantic content (§1.3).

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the document conforms to (semver). Renderers compare it with the maximum they support; see compatibility rule.

id.description: Stable identity of the brief across all of its versions (ULID).

version.description: Monotonically increasing per brief id, starting at 1. A frozen brief is never edited; a regeneration produces version + 1.

generated_at.description: When the brief was assembled and frozen (RFC 3339, with offset).

period_start.description: Start of the period the brief covers, inclusive (RFC 3339).

period_end.description: End of the period the brief covers, exclusive (RFC 3339). Must be greater than or equal to period_start; an empty period is representable (equal values).

language.description: Language of subject, summary and item prose as a BCP-47 tag (§4.2 requires sv, en, it and de to be evaluated). Quoted source excerpts may be in any language.

subject.description: Rendered as the mail subject and the menu bar headline. Plain text, single line.

summary.description: Short executive summary. Plain text; renderers must not truncate.

items.description: Ordered list of brief items. Order is semantic and must be preserved by every renderer.

sources.description: Every source referenced by any item. Each source names the connected account it came from (§5.6).

action_ids.description: Ids of action proposals (§11 approvals) created from this brief. Proposals are frozen, immutable objects owned by the approval module; this list is the link, not the proposal.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON of the content envelope: every top-level field except delivery_state, deliveries and content_hash itself. Renderers and parity tests use it to prove they rendered the same frozen content.

delivery_state.description: Lifecycle state. Ordered: draft < frozen < queued < sent | failed | skipped. From frozen onwards the content envelope is immutable.

idempotency_key.description: Assigned once at freeze time (ULID). Every delivery attempt of this version carries it; a retry must find an existing sent delivery with the same key, channel and recipient and skip sending (§1.3).

deliveries.description: Append-only log of delivery attempts per channel and recipient. At most one entry per (channel, recipient) may have status sent.

stale_after.description: After this instant the menu bar must show the brief as stale (§1.1). Must be greater than generated_at.

kind.description: action: the owner should do something; followup: a promised or expected follow-up; risk: something that may go wrong; info: context with no expected action; commitment: a commitment extracted from communication (§3.1 commitments).

body.description: Plain text. Quoted excerpts from sources are part of the body and may be in another language than the brief.

due_at.description: Only allowed when the deadline is present in a referenced source. Never inferred (§4.2: no invented deadlines).

source_refs.description: Ids of entries in the top-level sources array that substantiate this item.

action_ids.description: Subset of the top-level action_ids that originate from this item.

dedupe_key.description: Stable key for the underlying matter across email, CRM and GitHub so the same matter appears once (§4.2).

uncertainty.description: Explicit uncertainty marker for a material claim that has no source (§4.2). Renderers must display it visibly next to the item.

confidence.description: Model-reported confidence in [0, 1]. Informational; it never upgrades an unsourced claim to a sourced one.

uri.description: Locator of the original record. Resolvable inside the product (e.g. a message, CRM object or GitHub URL); never contains credentials.

account_id.description: The connected account (external_accounts id) the record was read from. Required for email, github and calendar; null for crm (local system of record), manual and ai_inference (§5.6: every action shows its source account).

account_label.description: Display label for the account, e.g. the mailbox address or GitHub org. Required by renderers whenever account_id is set; never a secret.

title.description: Human-readable title of the source record (mail subject, issue title, CRM object name).

captured_at.description: When the source record was read for this brief (RFC 3339).

excerpt_hash.description: SHA-256 of the exact excerpt used, so a reviewer can detect that the source changed after the brief was frozen.

if.$comment: Sources read from a connected external account must name that account (§5.6). crm is the local system of record and has no account; manual and ai_inference have none either.

modelProvenance.description: Which model produced the brief under which privacy mode. provider is none for a placeholder brief that was produced without any model.

provider.description: Adapter identifier (lowercase). none means no model was involved.

prompt_hash.description: SHA-256 of the full prompt (after redaction) so a run can be replayed against fixtures (§4 replay).

trace_id.description: Trace id of the ai_runs record that produced this version.

recipient.description: email: the approved recipient address (§5.5). menubar and pwa: the local surface identifier, e.g. menubar:local or pwa:local.

message_id.description: Provider or SMTP Message-ID for email, derived deterministically from idempotency_key, channel and recipient. Null until sent.

error.description: Sanitised error summary for failed attempts. Never contains credentials or message content.
